cases.initial_text: A predictive system can remain accurate on its training distribution while becoming unreliable after deployment. Changes in measurement procedures, class proportions, or the relationship between observations and outcomes create different forms of distribution shift. Evaluation should separate these mechanisms before choosing an adaptation strategy. Repeated measurements on representative data help distinguish persistent changes from sampling noise without assuming that a single aggregate accuracy captures every failure.

cases.initial_text: A replicated system must distinguish agreement about an operation from successful delivery of its result. Network delays can leave a client uncertain even when a quorum has accepted the write. Retrying with a stable request identifier allows the service to recognize duplicate work. This design separates the consistency protocol from the application response and makes recovery behavior explicit when a connection fails between commitment and acknowledgment.
